meta.title: Phase and progress — Palsya
meta.description: Your recovery stage, your logged sessions and how your stage has changed over time.

progress.pageSub: Three different things, kept separate because they measure different things and move at different speeds.
progress.noPhase: No stage has been assigned yet.
progress.threeThingsBody: There is no single "percent recovered" number, because there is no honest way to compute one. These three are what we can actually measure.
progress.arcAria: Progress across measured symmetry, sessions logged, and reported function
progress.observationsRecorded: {n, plural, one {# observation} other {# observations}} recorded
progress.threeArcsHint: Deliberately three separate arcs. A single combined figure would hide the case where the score is flat but you can suddenly drink from a glass — which is the case that matters most.
progress.noStreakHint: No streak, no target, no percentage. This is here so you and a clinician can see the pattern alongside the measurements.
progress.noScansBody: Your scores will be plotted here once scans are saved to your account. Until then this space stays empty rather than showing a number that wasn't measured.

meta.title: Progress report — Palsya
meta.description: A printable summary of your stage, your logged sessions and what you noticed.

report.title: Progress report
report.clinicalNote: everything in this report is self-reported by the patient — the session log and written observations — together with the stage the programme assigned. It contains no symmetry measurement, no prediction and no severity grade, and it does not map to House-Brackmann or Sunnybrook.

what.p: Everything below is drawn from your own sessions and notes between {from} and {to}. It contains no predictions and no clinical grading. It is written to be readable by you and useful to a clinician you share it with.

measurement.none: No scan has been stored on your account yet, so there is nothing measured to report.

programme.unchanged: Your stage has not changed since your assessment.

logged.p1: Over the last 28 days you logged {full, plural, one {# complete session} other {# complete sessions}} and {part, plural, one {# partial session} other {# partial sessions}}. Across the whole programme, {done, plural, one {# complete session} other {# complete sessions}}.
logged.p2: This is recorded so that you and a clinician can see the pattern alongside the measurements. It is not a score and nobody is grading it.

noticed.intro: You recorded these yourself, and they are often the part a clinician reads first:

not.h: What this report does not say
not.p: It does not predict your outcome, because no honest prediction is available from this data. It does not assign a clinical severity grade. And it does not compare you with other patients, because that comparison would tell you nothing useful about your own face.

meta.title: Session log — Palsya
meta.description: A calendar and list of the sessions you have logged.

log.title: Session log
log.pageSub: A record, not a scoreboard. It exists so you and a clinician can see the pattern next to the measurements.
log.emptyDaysHint: Empty days are just empty. There is no colour for "you failed".
log.nothingYet: Nothing yet. Function often changes before geometry does — "drank from a glass without holding my lip" is exactly the kind of thing worth writing down.

meta.title: Milestones — Palsya
meta.description: Factual observations from your own data.

milestones.title: Milestones
milestones.pageSub: Factual observations from your own data. No badges, no points, and nothing you can lose.
milestones.explainer: A milestone appears when something specific happens — a stage change, or a number of complete sessions. It never appears for effort, and it never disappears.
milestones.firstArrives: Your first milestone arrives with your first complete session.

firstSession.title: First full session complete
firstSession.body: You finished taping, exercises, and the daily routine in one day. That is the shape of every day from here.

sevenSessions.title: Seven full sessions
sevenSessions.body: Seven complete sessions logged. Consistency at this level is what the clinical evidence is built on.

thirtySessions.title: Thirty full sessions
thirtySessions.body: Thirty complete sessions. Most of the measurable change in facial rehabilitation happens across this kind of span.

stage.title: Moved to Stage {n} — {name}
stage.body: Your programme changed to match Stage {n}: the taping, exercises and routine you see now are the ones for this stage.
